summary: Riding a minecart cluster into a wall freezes the game
description: Derailed Minecarts that are clustered together often keep their movement speed, which is due to another bug (). In some cases (with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled) if such clusters of minecarts are ridden by the player and collide with blocks, the screen goes black and the game stops working. It then has to be terminated manually. Steps to reproduce (or use the link below for a more reliable method): - Place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail. - Push the minecarts. They should now start to move off the rail, keeping their velocity. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into blocks (2 blocks high is best). Water like in the attached videos isn t needed. This is not very reliable, so a few attempts may be needed. Alternatively, the attached world ( ) can be used to reproduce the bug: - Open the world. - Walk into the minecart cluster. - Ride one of the minecarts in the cluster. - Wait until it collides into the wall and locks the game.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
2. Enable the Minecart Improvements experiment in Options.
3. Place approximately 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail.
4. Push the minecarts so they start moving and eventually derail, maintaining their velocity.
5. Ride one of the derailing minecarts.
6. Wait until the cluster collides into blocks (a wall two blocks high is ideal).
7. Observe that the screen goes black and the game stops working, requiring manual termination.
Observed Behavior: When riding a cluster of derailed minecarts into a wall with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled, the game freezes. This issue occurs when the player rides one of the minecarts in the cluster as they collide with blocks, causing the screen to go black and the game to stop working, necessitating manual termination. To reproduce this bug, place around 20 to 30 minecarts on a normal rail and push them until they start moving off the rail while maintaining their velocity. Then, ride one of the minecarts in the cluster and wait for it to collide with blocks that are two blocks high. Alternatively, use an attached world where you can walk into the minecart cluster, ride one of the minecarts, and wait for it to collide with a wall, which locks up the game. This method is less reliable but may require multiple attempts to reproduce the issue consistently.
Expected Behavior: When riding a cluster of minecarts into a wall, the game should not freeze. Instead, the player should see the minecarts collide with the blocks normally, potentially scattering or stopping upon impact, without causing any visual glitches or gameplay interruptions. The screen should remain interactive, and the player should be able to continue playing without needing to manually terminate the game.
